title: slaptain — slapd
description: ADR-033 Surface 3, this site: each slapd pod's own cn=Monitor via the exporter sidecar — exporter and process health, connections and operations, threads, traffic, and LMDB per database. Scoped data source → namespace → cluster → role → pod → suffix.

links.title: slaptain — mesh state
links.tooltip: This site's mesh: CR state and the operator's replication judgments

options.content:
**slapd itself, per pod — Surface 3 of ADR-033.** slapd's own `cn=Monitor`, read on every scrape by the exporter sidecar and scraped through the operator chart's `slapdPodMonitor`. Empty unless the SlapdCluster has `spec.monitoring.enabled` **and** this site's operator chart has `slapdPodMonitor.enabled`. **This site only** — pick another site's data source to see it. Replication within this site — the operator's ReplicationConverged and the contextCSN spread behind it — is the row under the headline, for every cluster, with or without a meshRef; it needs kube-state-metrics and the operator's metrics, not the exporter. Cross-site links are on the *slaptain — mesh state* dashboard (link above).

**A missing line is not a zero.** A reading slapd could not give is absent from the scrape; the panels draw it as a gap. The families are the exporter's curated, typed table (ADR-033 decision 4, `docs/MONITORING.md`): counters end in `_total` and are drawn as rates. Rates use `$__rate_interval` with a 30 s floor, matching the PodMonitor's default interval.

panels.title: Pods with a cn=Monitor reading
panels.description: Share of the selected exporter targets whose last scrape reported openldap_up 1 — the exporter's own reading that it read cn=Monitor (a failed dial, bind or search sets it to 0 and drops every cn=Monitor family at once). Below 100% either an exporter target is down or slapd did not answer it — the 'cn=Monitor reading per pod' panel says which, and which pod. Empty when no exporter target is in scope at all.

defaults.noValue: no exporter target in scope — spec.monitoring.enabled or slapdPodMonitor.enabled is off

panels.title: Fullest data database
panels.description: Highest (pages_used − pages_free) / pages_max over the selected pods' data databases (every suffix except cn=accesslog-*; the node-local cn=slaptain-auth is included). Thresholds are the alert rules': SlaptainMDBMapFilling at 80%, SlaptainMDBMapNearlyFull at 90%. A full map refuses every write; olcDbMaxSize can only be raised by recreate (ADR-024).

panels.title: Fullest accesslog
panels.description: Highest map fill over the selected pods' cn=accesslog-* journals (read-write pods only — read-only pods keep no journal). Thresholds are the alert rules': SlaptainAccesslogMapFilling at 70%, SlaptainAccesslogMapNearlyFull at 85% — lower than for data databases, because a journal fills with write rate and purge age, not with directory size, and a full one stops every write to the database it journals.

defaults.noValue: no accesslog statistics in scope — read-only pods only, or no replicated database

panels.title: Busiest reader table
panels.description: Highest readers_used / readers_max over every selected pod × database. A reader slot is held per concurrent read transaction; when the table is full new reads fail. Threshold is the alert rule's (SlaptainMDBReaderSlotsHigh, 80%).

panels.title: Operations completed /s
panels.description: All operation types, all selected pods, from monitorOpCompleted (openldap_operations_completed_total). Includes slaptain's own background: every exporter scrape is a bind, a search and an unbind; every readiness probe a bind, a WhoAmI extended operation and an unbind; the operator's per-pod passes and the syncrepl consumers add searches.

panels.title: slapd restarts in range
panels.description: How many times a selected pod's slapd start time (openldap_start_time_seconds, from cn=Start,cn=Time) changed within the dashboard's time range: a slapd process restart, a container restart or a replaced pod alike. Counted per pod over the pod's merged series (a replaced pod gets a new instance label), so a pod rescheduled under the same name still counts. A restart that happened while the pod was not scraped at all is still seen, as long as a reading exists on either side of it.

panels.title: Replication within this site — per cluster × database
ReplicationConverged per cluster
panels.description:
The operator's judgment of whether every read-write pod of the cluster carries the same contextCSN vector, per database, AND-ed over databases (ADR-008 amendment). It compares pods of this site with each other, so every replicated cluster has it, with or without a meshRef; cross-site links are on the mesh state dashboard. The reason is part of the row label: CSNsDiverged is lag, CSNQueriesIncomplete is missing evidence — two different alerts.

From kube-state-metrics (Surface 1), so empty without it. The fleet, pod and database selectors do not apply.

defaults.noValue: no ReplicationConverged recorded for this cluster — kube-state-metrics is not scraping slaptain's CRs, or the cluster does not replicate

panels.title: contextCSN spread across pods
panels.description:
Newest minus oldest contextCSN timestamp across the read-write pods that answered, per database. This is the MAGNITUDE behind ReplicationConverged, which is an exact set comparison and so reads the same for half a second of propagation and for a pod frozen since yesterday.

**A gap in a line is not a zero.** The series is ABSENT below two readable pods, because a 0 there would read as perfect convergence for a measurement nobody took (ADR-033 decision 5). A measured 0 — two or more pods that agree — is drawn as a point on the zero line; an absent one leaves a hole, because spanNulls is off. If a line stops, read the CSN evidence panel beside it, not this one.

The operator's own metrics (Surface 2), so empty unless its chart has metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled. The fleet, pod and database selectors do not apply.

defaults.noValue: no spread measured anywhere in scope — fewer than two pods answered for every database, which is an absence of evidence and not a clean reading

panels.title: CSN evidence per database — pairs read of expected
panels.description:
The two absolute counts behind the ratio, per database. They are two counts rather than one ratio because a ratio has to divide by a count that can be 0. `read` dropping below `expected` while `expected` holds steady is pods going unreadable; both dropping together is a database leaving the pass.

A present 0 on `read` means every pair was attempted and every one failed — the attempt is the observation. An absent series means the pass never looked at that database at all.

defaults.noValue: no CSN pass recorded in scope

panels.title: cn=Monitor reading per pod
panels.description: Per selected pod: 'reading' — the exporter answered with openldap_up 1 and slapd's cn=Monitor families; 'slapd unreadable' — the exporter answered with openldap_up 0: its dial, bind or search of slapd failed or timed out (5s), so the scrape carried only openldap_up and the exporter's own counters (SlaptainSlapdMonitorUnreadable); 'exporter down' — Prometheus could not scrape the sidecar at all (SlaptainSlapdExporterDown). A gap is a pod with no target in that interval — not yet created, or gone.

defaults.noValue: no exporter target in scope — spec.monitoring.enabled or slapdPodMonitor.enabled is off

targets.expr: up{job="slapd-exporter",namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod"} + on (namespace, pod) group_left () (max by (namespace, pod) (openldap_up{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod"}) or max by (namespace, pod) (0 * up{job="slapd-exporter",namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod"}))

panels.title: Scrape duration per pod
panels.description: How long each exporter scrape took — dominated by the cn=Monitor read (dial, EXTERNAL bind over ldapi, one subtree search). The red line is the exporter's own --timeout (5s): a read still running then is abandoned and that scrape carries no cn=Monitor families. A climb here while slapd still answers is slapd itself getting slow; a frozen slapd (ADR-030) shows as a flat 5s.

panels.title: slapd uptime per pod
panels.description: time() − openldap_start_time_seconds (cn=Start,cn=Time) — seconds since this slapd process started. A drop to near zero is a restart; the stat above counts the start time's changes. A gap is a scrape without a cn=Monitor reading (see the state timeline), not a restart.

panels.title: Failed exporter dials and binds
panels.description: Failures per scrape interval of the exporter's own connection (openldap_exporter_dials_total) and SASL EXTERNAL bind (openldap_exporter_binds_total) to slapd. These counters are the exporter's, so they survive a slapd that cannot be read. The result="fail" series only exists once a first failure has happened, so a healthy exporter shows nothing here — that is the absence of any failure since the sidecar started, not a reading of zero. A frozen slapd shows as bind failures (the dial still succeeds).

defaults.noValue: no failed dial or bind since each selected exporter started

panels.title: Data database map fill
panels.description: (pages_used − pages_free) / pages_max per pod × database — the share of the map in use, against olcDbMaxSize. pages_used alone is a high-water mark that never shrinks after deletes; pages_free is what LMDB will reuse. Same expression and thresholds as the alert rules. A missing line is a database without statistics (opened before cn=Monitor existed — the pod's next restart attaches them), never an empty one. Data databases and the node-local cn=slaptain-auth; thresholds SlaptainMDBMapFilling (80%) and SlaptainMDBMapNearlyFull (90%).

panels.title: Accesslog map fill
panels.description: (pages_used − pages_free) / pages_max per pod × database — the share of the map in use, against olcDbMaxSize. pages_used alone is a high-water mark that never shrinks after deletes; pages_free is what LMDB will reuse. Same expression and thresholds as the alert rules. A missing line is a database without statistics (opened before cn=Monitor existed — the pod's next restart attaches them), never an empty one. The cn=accesslog-* journals of the read-write pods: they fill with write rate times purge age (accesslogPurge, docs/TUNING.md), not with directory size. Thresholds SlaptainAccesslogMapFilling (70%) and SlaptainAccesslogMapNearlyFull (85%).

defaults.noValue: no accesslog statistics in scope — read-only pods only, or no replicated database

panels.title: Databases now — one row per pod × database
panels.description: The latest reading of every selected database on every selected pod. Fill is the alert rules' ratio; 'in use' is (pages_used − pages_free) × page size and 'map size' pages_max × page size — the configured olcDbMaxSize — both empty on the -ol26 image, which reports no page size. Entries is olmMDBEntries; for one data suffix it should match across pods once replication has caught up, but whether it has is judged by contextCSN on the mesh dashboard, not by this count. Sort by any column.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, cluster, role, pod, suffix) ((openldap_mdb_pages_used{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"} - openldap_mdb_pages_free{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"}) / openldap_mdb_pages_max{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"})

max by (namespace, cluster, role, pod, suffix) ((openldap_mdb_pages_used{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"} - openldap_mdb_pages_free{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"}) * openldap_mdb_page_size_bytes{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"})

max by (namespace, cluster, role, pod, suffix) (openldap_mdb_pages_max{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"} * openldap_mdb_page_size_bytes{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"})
max by (namespace, cluster, role, pod, suffix) (openldap_mdb_entries{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"})
max by (namespace, cluster, role, pod, suffix) (openldap_mdb_readers_used{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"})
max by (namespace, cluster, role, pod, suffix) (openldap_mdb_readers_max{namespace="$namespace",cluster=~"$cluster",role=~"$role",pod=~"$pod",suffix=~"$suffix"})

panels.title: Entries per database per pod
panels.description: olmMDBEntries. For a data suffix the lines of all pods should coincide; a pod persistently apart is worth a look at the replication row above, which is the actual convergence judgment. A journal's count rises with writes and falls with each purge.

panels.title: Reader slots in use per pod × database
panels.description: readers_used / readers_max — the LMDB reader table, one slot per concurrent read transaction. Threshold is SlaptainMDBReaderSlotsHigh (80%). Slots of a crashed reader are reclaimed only when the environment is reopened.

panels.title: Current connections per pod
panels.description: openldap_connections_current (cn=Current,cn=Connections) — open client connections right now, including the syncrepl consumers of other pods and sites, the operator's per-pod sessions and the exporter's own. Read-only pods take only client and consumer-side traffic.

panels.title: New connections per second per pod
panels.description: Rate of openldap_connections_total (cn=Total,cn=Connections) — connections accepted. The steady floor is slaptain's own: one per exporter scrape and one per readiness probe. A storm of short-lived connections (a client without connection reuse, a reconnect loop) shows here before it shows anywhere else.

panels.title: Operations completed per second per pod
panels.description: Every operation type per pod (openldap_operations_completed_total, from monitorOpCompleted). A replication storm — a stale-cookie refresh loop — reads as hundreds of binds and searches per second on the affected pods while every signal in the replication row above stays flat. Completed only; openldap_operations_initiated_total is exported alongside it. The thread panels below show the queue.

panels.title: Operations per second by type and fleet
panels.description: The operation mix, summed over the selected pods of each fleet: read-write versus read-only. Searches and binds normally dominate; extended is mostly slaptain's readiness probe (WhoAmI). Comparing the fleets shows where client reads actually land.

panels.title: Write operations per second per pod
panels.description: Add, Modify, Delete and Modrdn per pod, as clients sent them (op=~"add|modify|delete|modrdn"). cn=Monitor counts client operations only: a change a pod applies through syncrepl counts nowhere, on a read-write consumer and a read-only pod alike. So this is not the rate an accesslog fills at — a read-write pod journals the changes it replicates in as well as its own, so its accesslog grows with the whole cluster's writes. That rate is the accesslog's line in 'Entries per database per pod'.

panels.title: Worker threads per pod
panels.description: openldap_threads_active (cn=Active) — threads executing an operation; openldap_threads_open (cn=Open) — threads that exist in the pool; the dashed line is openldap_threads_max (cn=Max, olcThreads), the pool's ceiling. Active pinned at Max with operations queuing (next panel) is saturation; Active far below Max with a queue is not.

panels.title: Queued operations per pod
panels.description: openldap_threads_pending (cn=Pending) — operations waiting for a worker thread; openldap_threads_backload (cn=Backload) — pending plus active, slapd's own load figure. Not alerted on: live it read above zero with only 2–9 of 16 threads active, so a non-zero queue is depth, not saturation. Sustained growth together with Active at Max is the signal.

panels.title: Waiters per pod
panels.description: openldap_waiters{direction="read"} (cn=Read,cn=Waiters) — connections idle, waiting for the client to send; roughly the open connections. cn=Write,cn=Waiters — connections whose results slapd cannot write because the client is not reading. Write waiters that persist mean slow or stuck clients holding threads.

panels.title: Bytes sent per second per pod
panels.description: Rate of openldap_sent_bytes_total (cn=Bytes,cn=Statistics) — everything slapd wrote to its clients, syncrepl consumers included. A full refresh to a consumer shows as a burst here on the providing pod.

panels.title: PDUs, entries and referrals sent per second per pod
panels.description: Rates of openldap_sent_{pdus,entries,referrals}_total (cn=PDU, cn=Entries and cn=Referrals under cn=Statistics). Entries sent per second is the read volume in directory terms — a search returning many entries counts once as an operation and many times here.
